short: Closed-loop formant decoding (M06) and F1/F2 output (M08) are standard: gesture-driven formant synthesis came first; one user learns vowels; hit rate lacks a chance level; no speech measured.
position: The paper [@guenther2009] closed the loop from motor cortex to sound (M06, Kalman filter to formants, audio 30–70 ms after neural firing) through two formants of a Klatt synthesizer (M08), and reports a transcutaneous telemetric implant (M13) whose priority over the group's earlier implants is unresolved. All three are standard: real-time control of a formant synthesizer from a non-acoustic signal predates it in hand-gesture systems [@fels2008], the neural source is the new part, and one participant with one electrode gives no repetition. The main claim, that a locked-in user learns to steer vowels, holds. Its measure is weak: the 45% to 70% hit rate from opening to closing block (Discussion) is helped by an attractor force and has no chance level or decoder-off control (Methods). Nothing measures speech, so "near-conversational" output (Abstract) is a projection; it is the protocol ancestor of the [later] sentence closed loop at a median 43.75% open-transcription WER [@wairagkar2025], not a performance reference.
